<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reviewing the notes garden's frontmatter conventions.

These fields are designed for atomic garden notes. Blogs are essay-length prose without a single core claim. They rely on description, related notes, and tags instead. Depth levels would not map cleanly to most blog types.

A site-wide requirement is not recommended. Idea or teaching posts might use these fields selectively. `related_notes` pointing to garden notes that already carry the depth ladder is the better bridge.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

**Mostly no** — not as a site-wide blog frontmatter standard.

`key_concept` + `level_1`…`level_5` are built for **one atomic claim**. The ladder (Recognize → Create) only works when the page is about a single idea. Notes are that shape; blogs usually aren’t.

| Fit | Examples |
|-----|----------|
| Poor | Alex Eala tracker, gear reviews, family stories, recipes — no single claim to level |
| Awkward | Most opinion posts — the *body* is the claim; duplicating it in frontmatter fights Zinsser/jorap-voice |
| Maybe | Idea/teaching posts that are basically an expanded garden note |

What you already have covers the bridge:

- Blog `description` = the one-breath hook (SEO + list cards)
- `related_notes` = link to garden notes that already own the depth stack
- Body prose = where depth shows up (lived example → tradeoff → what you’d do)

Duplicating the five-level stack on blogs would mean maintaining the same claim in two places, and half the archive wouldn’t earn honest Level 4–5 lines.

**If you still want structure on some posts**, keep it optional and narrow — e.g. only when a post is “one idea, taught hard,” and prefer pointing at a note rather than copying `level_1`…`level_5` into the blog. A single optional `key_concept` one-liner for card/search blurbs is cheaper than the full ladder, and still mostly overlaps `description`.

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Use a **single integer in frontmatter**, not a Hugo tag.

```yaml
depth: 3   # max rung this post reaches: 1–5
```

| Value | Rung | Rough blog signal |
|------:|------|-------------------|
| 1 | Recognize | Names the idea / news scrapbook |
| 2 | Explain | Teaches what it means |
| 3 | Use | Shows you applying it |
| 4 | Connect | Tradeoffs, systems, links across ideas |
| 5 | Create | You invent / ship / extend from it |

Why not `tags: ["Level 3"]`: tags are topical and public (`/tags/…`). Depth is metadata for filtering and your own ranking, same family as `featured` / `related_notes`.

**Meaning:** highest level the *post reaches*, not the reader’s level. Alex Eala tracker ≈ **1**; a how-I-built post that ships a system ≈ **4–5**.

Want me to add `depth` to `BLOG_FM_ORDER`, a small lint (`1–5` or omit), and optionally a quiet badge on the post — without backfilling every file yet?

cd /home/jorap/Documents/GitHub/jorap.com && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
root = Path('content/english/blog')
for p in sorted(root.glob('*.md')):
    if p.name == '_index.md':
        continue
    text = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    if not text.startswith('---'):
        print(f'{p.name}\tNO_FM')
        continue
    end = text.find('\n---', 3)
    fm = text[3:end]
    def get(key):
        m = re.search(rf'^{key}:\s*(.*)$', fm, re.M)
        if not m: return ''
        v = m.group(1).strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        return v
    title = get('title')
    desc = get('description')
    draft = get('draft')
    cats = re.search(r'^categories:\s*\[(.*?)\]', fm, re.M)
    cats = cats.group(1) if cats else ''
    print(f'{p.name}\t{draft}\t{title}\t{desc[:100]}\t{cats[:60]}')
PY
